thread_text:
incident-bot: Pager: increased 5xxs for /v1/complete (eu-central-1). Error signature: "column "settings_v2" does not exist". Paging oncall (sam). :rotating_light:

sam: I see the 500 spikes. App logs show stacktrace from profile-service when reading settings_v2. Canary was rolled ~12m ago.

anika: canary details: deploy d-2025-03-02-12, migration job mig-77 launched as part of release. CI says migration started but a couple of runners failed with timeout acquiring exclusive lock.

devon: the migration adds JSONB column settings_v2 and a GIN index. Looks like some pods already have new binary expecting the column. Partial schema state.

mike: deploy-bot shows mig-77 restarted 3 times due to K8s job restarts; no leader election. Could be racing DDLs.

sam: immediate mitigation: disable code path that reads new column. Which feature flag guards the new settings?

anika: ff:settings/v2-read. Flipping now via config-api. `POST /flags/settings/v2-read {"value":false}` -> 200.

incident-bot: feature flag updated by anika at 2025-03-02T12:14:11Z :white_check_mark:

devon: traffic 5xx down from 11% to 1.6% in last 3m. But migration job still failing and occasionally spawning new pods which try DDL again. Need to stop mig-77.

mike: I can patch job: `kubectl patch job mig-77 -n migrations -p '{"spec":{"parallelism":0}}'` and annotate `migrated=false` so controller doesn't retry. Want me to run?

sam: yes run it. Also block outgoing worker traffic to DB from migration pods if they respawn: `kubectl label pods -l job-name=mig-77 paused=true -n migrations` is fine.

mike: patched job parallelism=0 and labeled existing pods. deploy-bot: job mig-77 paused.

anika: good. Still see a few app pods throwing errors because they were warm and have old config. Rolling restart should clear them but we should be careful not to drop traffic.

devon: can we cordon only the pods with new binary? `kubectl get pods -l app=profile-service,version=new -o name` then rollout restart.

sam: go ahead with a gradual restart - 10% at a time. Keep ff off.

incident-bot: customer impact update: peak 5xx rate 11% in eu-central-1, ~7 minutes of elevated errors; two paying customers reported failed requests.

support: opening tickets for affected customers, adding temporary mitigation note.

anika: why did this slip through canary? Canary logs show no DB errors. I suspect canary didn't execute the backfill code path. Might have been a config drift where canary pods used older env var set.

devon: confirmed: canary group had env VAR SET USE_OLD_SETTINGS=true, so the canary never hit the new read path. That explains false positive.
sam: this is a process gap—canary should mirror prod flags and env. Add to postmortem.

mike: next steps for remediation: 1) ensure all app instances stop reading settings_v2 (flag off) 2) ensure migration job won't run concurrent DDLs (add leader lease) 3) clear DB schema locks and then perform migration in controlled single-leader mode 4) backfill with throttling then flip flag and roll forward.

anika: for clearing locks, I'm checking blocking sessions: `SELECT pid, state, query, now() - query_start AS age FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%LOCK%' OR state='idle in transaction';` I see one long-running analytics query > 50m.

devon: we need to coordinate with analytics, but this is high priority. oncall-sre, page analytics lead; if no response in 2m, we should terminate sessions.

oncall-sre: paging analytics-lead now. No ack; terminating offending pids in 90s unless they respond.

incident-bot: termination executed by devon at 2025-03-02T12:28:40Z. Locks released.

mike: with locks gone, we can try a dry-run of migration on a single leader node with explicit leader-election. I'll modify the job to run `--leader-lock` and `--no-index` first. After verifying add-column succeeds across replicas, we'll run index creation CONCURRENTLY and then backfill.

anika: good plan. Also add a preflight that checks for live long transactions and refuses to start if any exist.

sam: customer comms: Draft message: "We observed elevated 500s caused by a partially-applied database migration during a rolling deploy. We disabled the new settings read path and paused the migration. Service has returned to normal; we will schedule a controlled migration and follow up with details." I'll post to #customer-notifications after review.

support: customers notified with the draft; two orgs opened priority tickets; CS assigned owners.
devon: handoff: I'm primary for the next 45m, then anika takes over. sam please add handoff note in #oncall-handoffs.

sam: will do. Also creating INFRA-5042 for migration leader-election, PM task PM-2187 to enforce canary parity, and OBS-891 to alert on long-running DDLs.

incident-bot: SLO impact summary: 7 minutes degraded, peak 11% 5xx, incident mitigated at 2025-03-02T12:33:02Z. Please file full postmortem and link INFRA-5042. :white_check_mark:

anika: one more thing—some users may have had partial updates during the brief window before FF flip. We'll run a reconciliation job to detect nulls in settings_v2 and backfill defaults for consistency.

mike: scheduling the safe migration window during low traffic tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Will coordinate with analytics for no-long-transaction guarantee.

sam: thanks all. Good quick response. Post-incident TODOs: enforce canary-env parity, leader locks for migrations, migration preflight checks, and test FF kill-switch latency.

incident-bot: incident closed by sam at 2025-03-02T12:36:22Z.
